findings: 10214080 raises start/end/aim to max(target-column ground + authored target height, relative-rise field). It forms the length15 intermediate on the raised start-to-end line, then adds12 only to start.Y. The native comparison to relative rise is retained despite its unusual world-height behavior.

10213620 additionally raises end.Y by a Distance=30 terrain square query. Authored UseTargetIntermediate=false computes start+normalize(end-start)*15, then replaces intermediate.Y with raised aim.Y before adding12 to start.Y.

103bbbe0 uses XZ projection with epsilon1e-10: before start uses XZ squared distance, inside subtracts projected squared length, at/beyond end uses full3D squared distance. Target validity compares absolute difference of that helper for current versus cached target to10^2; height is compared separately to raisedAimY-targetHeight. It is not a movement-radius test.

Prepare tick state1 waits for movement to finish, validates and enters state2; state2 requires horizontal facing AND finished movement then validates, enters state3 and resets elapsed. State3 increments float elapsed and validates each tick; returns finished only when elapsed is strictly greater than0.5. The transition into waiting does not consume elapsed time.

Tight begin starts directly at state3 outbound, not states1/2. Outbound completion may enter state4 turn if GoBack and target validation succeed. Turn requires facing plus target validation, not another movement completion query; it enters state5 return to start through the same stored intermediate. Return completion ends the action.

While outbound is not completed,10213ef8 compares the squared helper result to literal40, not40^2. There is no matching per-tick gate on return. This is preserved; the helper is not changed to a conventional symmetric flight corridor.

103b83b0 considers only movement statuses2 and3 unfinished.103bab40 checks normalized horizontal forward dot strictly greater than float0.97. Native forward is negated actor basis; Java API accepts an already world-oriented forward vector.

Independent review found that Minecraft Vec3.normalize zeros short directions below1e-4 length, unlike107badf0 using squared epsilon approximately1e-10. Intermediate construction now explicitly divides by length and rejects nonfinite length from coordinate overflow.

adaptations: Vec3/double arithmetic replaces x86 float/x87 arithmetic; not claimed bit-exact.
Nonfinite inputs, degenerate route and invalid dt are rejected at the Java boundary.
READY/DONE versus ABORTED is a Java distinction; original callbacks return false for both finishing and invalidation.
Temporary target modes, source steering messages and movement statuses are not reimplemented here.
